nodes.label: Primary Model Training and Evaluation (spec)
nodes.rationale: A naive random split would put household or cluster members on both sides and inflate performance, a single accuracy number would hide class imbalance and miscalibration, and no subgroup reporting would hide poor performance for men, older adults, or poorer households. So the pipeline must be leakage-free, baseline-compared, sensitivity-first, calibrated, and honestly reported as aggregate results plus a model bundle that can later be served without redistributing microdata.

nodes.label: Cluster-Grouped Split Strategy
nodes.rationale: The primary grouping unit is the cluster (PSU) because keeping clusters intact blocks both household and community leakage. A 20% cluster-grouped holdout is created first, the remaining 80% is developed with 5-fold cluster-grouped CV, splitting is stratified on target and sex where feasible, and the pipeline asserts no cluster or household crosses a split or fold. Household-grouped splitting stays available as a configurable sensitivity check. The test set is untouched until selection, calibration, and threshold tuning finish, so those steps cannot peek.

nodes.label: 32-Feature State-Free Primary Feature Policy
nodes.rationale: The deployed model uses 32 of the 35 model-input columns. state is excluded to reduce local access- and diagnosis-pattern leakage; religion and social_group are excluded because they are sensitive attributes. State, fairness, and combined variants (33/34/35 features) exist so the impact of those exclusions is measured rather than assumed. Identifiers, cluster/household/line, PSU, strata, weights, target components, age_15_49, and the raw sex/residence encodings are never inputs; female and urban are the binary encodings used. Nominal categoricals use LightGBM native handling, ordinal variables stay ordered integers, and validation raises on forbidden or missing columns.

nodes.label: Three Baselines and Validation-Only Model Selection
nodes.rationale: Three models are required: a prevalence-only floor, a logistic regression with imputation/encoding/scaling and balanced weights, and LightGBM with native categoricals, missing-value support, class weighting, and early stopping. PR-AUC ranks on development CV and Brier/log loss break ties, because accuracy would reward the majority class and a well-ranked but poorly calibrated model is unacceptable for a screener. Tuning stays inside training folds and the test set is evaluated once after a refit on the full development set. Weighted training is a sensitivity analysis only, so probabilities stay individual-level.

nodes.label: Out-of-Fold Isotonic vs Platt Calibration
nodes.rationale: Calibration is essential because the product displays probabilities: a predicted 20% risk must mean roughly 20%. Isotonic and Platt are both fitted on out-of-fold development predictions and the winner is chosen by Brier score and log loss rather than by convention. The report shows reliability curves before and after, slope, intercept, Brier, log loss, and ECE, unweighted and survey-weighted, and by wealth, sex, and state where subgroup sizes permit.

nodes.label: Sensitivity-First Screening Threshold (target 80%)
nodes.rationale: The screener rules people in for further testing, so the default operating point maximises specificity subject to at least 80% sensitivity, ties broken by PPV, and the target is configurable for clinics with different referral capacity. The threshold is selected on out-of-fold development predictions, never on the test set; 0.5 is reported only for reference, and sensitivity at 80% specificity is reported as a threshold-independent model comparison.

nodes.label: Metrics and PSU-Clustered Bootstrap Intervals
nodes.rationale: Confidence intervals resample PSUs (default 1,000 replicates) so uncertainty reflects the survey design instead of pretending respondents are independent; small subgroups may use fewer replicates. Unweighted metrics are primary and survey-weighted metrics are a sensitivity analysis, so sample performance and population performance are distinguished. The weight is never treated as a sample-size multiplier, and all metrics are computed from calibrated probabilities.

nodes.label: Subgroup and Fairness Audit
nodes.rationale: Required subgroups are sex, age band, wealth quintile, residence, education, and state (with at least 500 test respondents); religion and social group are audit-only because they are not deployed features. Sex-specific metrics are mandatory because the pooled sample is roughly 88% female, and every row carries n, positives, and prevalence so small groups are not overinterpreted. Groups under 200 respondents or 50 positives are flagged unreliable and never used to claim fairness. The report states that removing a protected attribute does not make a model fair and that gaps are descriptive, not causal; this spec audits fairness and does not mitigate it.

nodes.label: SHAP Global and Local Explanations
nodes.rationale: SHAP runs on a fixed 5,000-row test sample so the run stays tractable, and a local explanation function returns a single respondent's top contributing features with direction and impact for the future API. Explanations are described as associations, not causes. If SHAP is unavailable the pipeline falls back to permutation or native LightGBM gain importance and records the fallback.

nodes.label: Run Artifacts and Schema-Validated Model Bundle
nodes.rationale: Each run writes to a unique timestamp/seed/hash directory with split assignment, resolved config, metadata, metrics, subgroup metrics, calibration curve, threshold analysis, feature importance, SHAP data, report, model card, and bundle. The bundle carries the fitted model, calibrator, feature and categorical columns, threshold, target definition, sample metadata, versions, and run id, so inference cannot silently diverge from training. The bundle is local-only and gitignored while aggregate outputs are publishable; the loader validates the schema and does not reimplement preprocessing.

nodes.label: Reproducibility, Python 3.11/3.12, and No Microdata Publication
nodes.rationale: Seeds, resolved config, dataset fingerprint, row/column counts, prevalence, package versions, and git commit are recorded so a result can be traced and repeated. Modeling targets Python 3.11 or 3.12 because LightGBM and SHAP wheels may lag on 3.14 (a premise later corrected by the review-cleanup amendment). A small-sample smoke mode keeps the full pipeline exercisable, and raw/processed microdata and model binaries are never committed.

nodes.label: End-to-End Integration Test at the Pipeline Seam
nodes.rationale: Tests assert externally observable behaviour - leakage-free splits, numerically correct metrics, in-range probabilities, a threshold that meets its sensitivity target on separable data, and a reloaded bundle reproducing predictions - rather than tree structures or column order. One integration test drives run_training_pipeline with a 300-500 row synthetic table and small config under about 60 seconds, while deterministic pure helpers (splits, metrics, calibration, threshold, subgroups, feature policy, artifact round-trip) are tested directly. No network, DVC, or GPU; real-data training is verified by manual smoke run.

nodes.label: Deferred Scope: Ensembles, Deployment, PR BP Model
nodes.rationale: Out of scope: the PR 15+ BP sensitivity model and its PR feature builder (a separate spec), the questionnaire-only, deployed state-specific and combined models beyond sensitivity roles, a 5-fold x 10-seed ensemble, large-scale hyperparameter search, FastAPI/demo/Docker/deployment, external and clinical validation, causal inference, fairness mitigation, small-area estimates, ONNX/mobile export, and redistributing microdata. A single-seed 5-fold run is the required implementation; the remaining variants follow once the pipeline is proven.
